summary: MARS EXPLORER is an interactive web-based Martian map prototype designed to help users explore the challenges of navigating and surviving on the surface of Mars. It presents illustrative terrain locations, potential hazards, science points, and a conceptual route through an easy-to-use interface. The project aims to demonstrate how an interactive map can support mission planning, exploration, and awareness of Martian surface conditions.
details:
MARS EXPLORER – Interactive Martian Survival Map

1. What does the project do?

MARS EXPLORER is an interactive web-based prototype designed to demonstrate how explorers can study and understand the Martian surface before planning exploration activities.

It provides an illustrative map containing different Martian terrain locations, potential hazard areas, scientific points of interest, and a conceptual exploration route. Users can interact with map markers, explore location information, and enable or disable different map layers.

2. How does it work?

The project uses a simple interactive interface. Users can select different locations on the map to view their descriptions. They can toggle terrain, hazard, and science-point layers, view a conceptual route, and use a Marswalk preparation checklist.

The interface is designed to make exploring Martian surface information simple and understandable.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

The project demonstrates how interactive mapping can help people understand the challenges of exploring Mars. It aims to:

  • Improve awareness of Martian terrain and exploration challenges.
  • Demonstrate how potential hazards and scientific locations can be presented visually.
  • Help users understand the importance of planning before surface exploration.
  • Provide an accessible educational tool for students and space enthusiasts.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

The prototype was developed using:

  • HTML – webpage structure.
  • CSS – visual design and responsive layout.
  • JavaScript – interactive features and map controls.
  • Web browser – running and testing the application.
  • GitHub Pages – public hosting of the project.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of MARS EXPLORER is its combination of an interactive Martian map, exploration locations, hazard layers, a conceptual route, and a preparation checklist in one simple interface.

Instead of presenting information only through text, the project demonstrates how users can explore different aspects of Mars through an interactive experience.

6. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered simplicity, accessibility, ease of navigation, responsive design, and the importance of presenting exploration information clearly.

Scientific accuracy is also an important consideration. The current version uses illustrative locations, routes, and hazard information for demonstration purposes. These are not verified NASA measurements or real mission navigation recommendations. Integrating georeferenced NASA datasets and verified scientific information is an important future development goal.

7. Future Improvements

Future versions could integrate authentic NASA and planetary science datasets, more accurate terrain information, verified hazard layers, and improved route-planning capabilities to make the project more useful for understanding real Mars exploration challenges.

8. SI Assistance Disclosure

ChatGPT was used to assist with code drafting, project description, and presentation organization. The team is responsible for reviewing, testing, understanding, and verifying the submitted project.
